synopsis: NRC Regulatory Guide 1.203, dated December 2005, defines the nuclear-domain Evaluation Model Development and Assessment Process (EMDAP) as four elements comprising 20 steps [f14642, f8088]. Its continued application to new reactor designs is illustrated by a 2025 safety evaluation of a TerraPower topical report and a related 2024 audit plan [f7660]. Experimental databases remain fundamental: PIRT ranks phenomena, with highly ranked phenomena requiring integral and separate-effects test data and lower-ranked phenomena receiving reduced emphasis [f7662, f7836]. Predictions outside the assessment matrix or physical scale require explicit scaling and applicability justification and uncertainty treatment; scale distortion and test uncertainty must not be hidden in a global correlation [f7661, f7663]. NRC also separates calibration from independent validation: agreement with a calibration test does not demonstrate predictive capability on independent data [f8159].

relations.note: Both identify NRC RG 1.203 EMDAP and its December 2005 date.
The 2024 audit and 2025 evaluation illustrate continued application of the 2005 guide.
Recent reactor evaluations illustrate continuing use of the defined EMDAP process.
Required test data for highly ranked phenomena explain why experimental databases remain fundamental.
Phenomena ranking and differentiated test requirements detail how EMDAP operates.
Specifies scale distortion and test uncertainty that applicability justification must address.
Clarifies that calibration data alone cannot establish independent predictive capability.
